newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian industrialists say no growth in output.
newsitem.headline: Colombian industrialists say no growth in output.

text.p: Colombia's industrial output showed no growth in the first-half of this year, but at least it is not continuing to fall as it did in the first few months of 1997, a new survey by the country's leading industrial association showed Friday.

The National Association of Industrialists (ANDI) said the growth in industrial output was nil in the first six months of the year compared with the same period last year. The growth in sales in the first-half was up just 0.3 percent compared with the first six months of 1996.
"We can say that the fall in output that we were seeing has stopped but between that and saying a recovery has started there's a huge gap," ANDI chairman Luis Carlos Villegas told a press conference.
Villegas said he believed a recovery may get underway in the second half of this year led by coffee and a return of investment in the industrial sector.

The ANDI's monthly survey showed that drinks, textiles, cements, rubber products and plastics were still suffering from the effects of recession. At least 78 percent of industrialists surveyed said they thought the outlook was mediocre or bad. The lack of demand was still the major obstacle, according to 34 percent of those polled, followed by slow turnover and low profit margins.
